g.text: Two encoder motors, four servo ports, IMU
Parallel lift with a gear-linked gripper
A classroom robot designed and built in Zambia. Its RoboCore V2 controller puts an ESP32-S3 with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, two
encoder motor drives, four servo ports, a motion sensor and sockets for line and ultrasonic sensing on one board, running from
1S lithium cells with USB-C charging. The robot arrives assembled, with its lift and gripper fitted.
Two encoder motors, four servo ports, IMU
Parallel lift with a gear-linked gripper

RoboCore robot, assembled: printed frame, lift and gripper with 2 micro servos, RoboCore V2 controller, 2 encoder motors, HC-SR04 ultrasonic, 3-channel line sensor, 4 V-wheels and the battery cradle · USB-C cable · Screw pack · Quick-start
Controller RoboCore V2, ESP32-S3, 68 x 60 mm
Power 1S Li-ion, 3 x 18650 in parallel, USB-C charging
Drive 2 x DG01D-E encoder motors, 56 mm wheels, 4 V-wheels
Sensing 3-channel line sensor, HC-SR04 ultrasonic, IMU
Robot 154 x 286 x 111 mm (lift level), about 620 g
Box 303 x 213 x 91 mm, E-flute card
Not a toy. Contains small parts and screws: not for children under 8. Use only 1S lithium cells; charge through
USB-C under supervision. Keep metal away from the antenna.
A robot a class can build, program and repair
OUTSIDE. RoboCore mailer box, roll-end tuck-top, outer 303 x 213 x 91 mm, E-flute 1.5 mm. Print 1:1; navy solid = cut, grey dashed = fold. Bar = 100 mm.
